title: Struct miscellany
recap: Structs can contain other struct objects, creating a hierarchy of related data. Chained member selection follows those nested objects.
Avoid assuming an object's memory size equals the sum of member sizes: implementations may add padding. Access members by name rather than by raw offsets.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement movePlayer(player,dx,dy), changing only the nested position coordinates of the caller's Player. Preserve name and health exactly. Position is a nested program-defined member type, not an independent global position variable. Sums fit int.
expectedOutput: Player{"Ada",{2,3},90} moved by (4,-1) -> position {6,2}, name/health unchanged
hints: Select player.position before its x or y member.
Do not reconstruct Player and accidentally reset name or health.
